generatedProse.concept-context: Whatever you are studying, the category is set by the brief, not by the subject. A brief in your field might set Category 1 and expect the work entirely in your own words, or Category 2 and let you take a structure from AI as long as you rewrite, reference and declare it. Reading the brief for its category is the habit that protects you. Permission to use AI, where it is given, is never permission to submit the tool's work as your own.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students working to the same brief, writing up a study, which sets Category 2: AI Acknowledged.

{{learner-a}} skims the brief, sees that AI is allowed, and pastes a chatbot's draft into the work almost unchanged, with no acknowledgement. Category 2 asks for the ideas to be rewritten, referenced and declared, so {{learner-a}} has gone beyond what the brief allows and is at risk of misconduct.

{{learner-b}} reads the brief properly, notes it is Category 2, and uses AI only to suggest a structure. {{learner-b}} then writes the work in their own words, references the sources, and adds a short statement of how AI was used. The same brief, done within its category.

Both were allowed to use AI. Only {{learner-b}} did what the category actually required.
generatedProse.summary: Cardiff Met sets three categories of AI use, and your assignment brief tells you which applies: Category 1, No Use of Generative AI Expected; Category 2, AI Acknowledged; and Category 3, AI Embedded. Your first move is always to read the brief for its category. Category 1 allows AI only for spelling, grammar and referencing; Category 2 lets you learn or get guidance from AI if you rewrite, reference and declare it; Category 3 builds AI into the task itself. Above all, permission to use AI is never permission to submit AI's work as your own. The next lesson looks at what counts as misconduct.

check.body: A brief in {{context}} says nothing at all about AI. Which category should you assume, and what does it allow?

items.text: Category 1: treat AI as not expected, and use it only to check spelling, grammar and referencing.
Category 3: AI is embedded, so use it freely across the task.
Category 2: use AI for anything, as long as you add a declaration.
Any category you like, because the brief did not rule AI out.

feedback.correct: That's right. If the brief is silent, treat it as Category 1 and keep AI to spelling, grammar and referencing checks.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Silence means Category 1 - no AI expected beyond spelling, grammar and referencing.
